shadows.name: overlay-lg

motion.name: reveal-on-scroll
motion.value: .reveal-on-scroll utility: opacity:1 by default; @supports (animation-timeline: view()) + prefers-reduced-motion:no-preference layers in a scroll-driven opacity+translate keyframe animation
motion.purpose: New this wave. CSS-only replacement for the five per-section IntersectionObserver hooks; not yet adopted by components (that's wave 3a's job).

motion.name: reveal-fade-slide (legacy, still live)
motion.value: opacity-0 translate-y-4 -> opacity-100 translate-y-0, transition-all duration-1000
motion.purpose: Still driven by IntersectionObserver + useState in Hero/About/Work/Experience/Contact as of this wave; to be deleted once .reveal-on-scroll is adopted.

motion.name: hover-color
motion.purpose: Default hover treatment on nearly all text links and nav items. No longer force-collapsed under prefers-reduced-motion (see reduced-motion note).

motion.name: cta-invert
motion.purpose: Hero primary CTA border-to-fill inversion and the error-page retry button.

motion.name: reduced-motion-reconciled
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce now clamps animation-duration/iteration-count only, not transition-duration
motion.purpose: Fixed this wave: the previous blanket rule also killed hover and theme-toggle color transitions, which the audit rubric flagged as an anti-pattern.

components.name: Primary Button (Hero CTA)
components.description: Outlined-to-filled CTA, the only filled-button interaction pattern in the build; most other CTAs are plain text links. Unchanged this wave except its focus ring now resolves through the shared token.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-block; padding: 12px 24px; border: 2px solid #1a1a1a; color: #1a1a1a; background: transparent; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; transition: all 0.3s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #1a1a1a; color: #fafafa; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0c6e66; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Text Link (default CTA)
components.description: The dominant interactive pattern site-wide: plain text with an accent-color hover, used for nav items, project 'Details ansehen' links, and contact rows. Now gets a visible focus-visible outline by default (previously absent on nearly all of these).

components.name: Tech Chip
components.description: Bordered, unfilled tag used to list project tech stacks. No background fill, no rounded corners. Its text color is the retuned `secondary` (#666666) — this is the specific element the accessibility audit flagged failing AA (4.3:1) before this wave.

components.name: Project Row
components.description: The closest thing to a 'card' in the build: no background fill or shadow, just a bottom hairline border separating stacked entries. Unchanged this wave; paragraph text now capped to 70ch measure.

narrative.overview: This is a single-page, section-scrolling personal portfolio (Hero, About, Work, Experience, Contact) plus three GitHub-README-backed project detail pages. The visual system is unstyled-by-intent minimalism: a near-black-on-off-white palette, one deep-teal accent used sparingly for links and hover states, no imagery beyond a single profile photo, no illustration, no gradients, and almost no shadows. This wave closed the two gaps that made the site read as an untouched framework starter: the font stack is now IBM Plex Sans (self-hosted, two weights, a real 1.25-ratio modular scale) instead of bare system-ui, and the accent is a deliberately chosen deep teal instead of Tailwind's unmodified blue-600. Dark mode still expresses itself through the Tailwind zinc-* scale at every component call site (that would require a component-editing pass to change), but every zinc stop the app depends on is now pinned explicitly in the same @theme block as the light-mode tokens rather than left as an implicit default, and the one real drift bug (a hardcoded dark-mode body background diverging from the zinc-950 value components actually use) has been closed. A token-driven focus-visible ring now reaches every interactive element, and a CSS-only .reveal-on-scroll utility is ready for the next wave to adopt in place of five duplicated IntersectionObserver hooks.
keyCharacteristics: Two-tone-plus-one-accent palette: near-black text, off-white background, single deep-teal accent used only on links/hover/active states and the focus ring.
One self-hosted typeface (IBM Plex Sans, two weights) carrying a deliberate 1.25-ratio modular scale.
No card surfaces, no drop shadows on content (only shadow-lg on the two overlay/dialog surfaces).
Hairline borders (1px) remain the primary structural device; their sub-3:1 contrast is a documented, deliberate trade-off, not an oversight.
Large, generous section rhythm: ~128-160px of vertical padding per full-height section, with a max-w-3xl content column - confirmed, not redesigned.
A token-driven :focus-visible outline and a CSS-only scroll-reveal utility now exist for every future interactive element/section to use.

rules.name: The One-Accent Rule
rules.body: The accent (accent / accent-muted) appears only on interactive elements - links, hover states, active nav indicators, focus rings, code accents. It never appears as a background fill, a section header color, or a decorative element. Unchanged this wave; only the hue moved from blue to teal.

rules.name: The Explicit Dark-Scale Rule
rules.body: Dark mode still expresses itself through Tailwind's zinc-* utility classes at every component call site - that could not change without editing every component. What changed: every zinc stop the app depends on is now pinned explicitly inside the same @theme block as the light-mode tokens, and the one place light and dark values had actually drifted apart (a hardcoded dark body background) has been closed.

rules.name: The Border-Contrast Caveat
rules.body: border and the dark zinc-800/zinc-700 borders measure well under the 3:1 UI-component floor. Treated as decorative content separators (WCAG 1.4.11 exempts graphical objects not required to identify a component), consistent with the Border-Not-Shadow Rule - not fixed by darkening, which would be a visible redesign. One exception (the ReadmeDropdown disclosure toggle's boundary) is flagged, unresolved, for wave 3a.

rules.name: The Uppercase-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Every section is introduced by a text-sm uppercase tracking-wider label in the secondary/muted color before its bold headline. Unchanged.

rules.name: The Modular-Scale Rule
rules.body: Every text-lg through text-7xl step is 1rem x 1.25^n for a fixed integer n, declared once in @theme and inherited by every component using these existing utility names - replacing the arbitrary, undocumented jumps the previous DESIGN.md flagged.

rules.name: The Max-Width-3XL Rule
rules.body: All five homepage sections share one max-w-3xl reading column, centered with w-full. Only the project detail template widens to max-w-4xl. Unchanged.

rules.name: The 70ch Measure Rule
rules.body: Any paragraph-length text block using leading-relaxed and not already constrained by its own max-w-* utility is capped to 70ch - closing the 85-96 characters-per-line defect the audit measured, without touching any component's max-w-3xl/max-w-4xl section width.

rules.name: The Border-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth and separation within the page flow is conveyed by a single hairline border, never a shadow or a tonal surface change. Shadows are reserved exclusively for the two modal/overlay surfaces. Unchanged.

dos: Do keep the accent teal (#0c6e66 / #59a69a) confined to interactive states (links, hover, focus, active nav indicator) - it does not appear as a fill or section color anywhere in the build.
Do use hairline 1px borders (border-border / dark:border-zinc-800) as the default separator between content blocks; reserve shadow-lg for true overlay surfaces (modal, mobile drawer) only.
Do keep homepage sections on the shared max-w-3xl column with py-32/lg:py-40 vertical rhythm and px-6/md:px-12 horizontal rhythm.
Do treat text-links as the default CTA pattern; the bordered outline-to-fill button exists as a single accent for the Hero's primary action, not a general button system.
Do use .reveal-on-scroll for any new scroll-triggered entrance instead of a fresh IntersectionObserver - it is CSS-only, visible-by-default, and already handles no-JS/no-support/reduced-motion.
Do rely on the baseline :focus-visible rule for new interactive elements rather than adding another one-off focus-visible:ring-* utility.
donts: Don't read secondary/zinc-500 as still being Tailwind's stock neutral-500/zinc-500 - both were deliberately retuned this wave to clear WCAG AA as real content.

Don't assume dark mode inherits the light-mode custom token names (primary, background, surface, border) - every dark: variant still reaches for raw zinc-* utility classes; only the values backing those utilities are now a single declared source of truth.

Don't darken border/zinc-800/zinc-700 to chase a 3:1 UI-component ratio without deciding to redesign the whole hairline-divider visual language - treat the current values as a deliberate, documented trade-off, except for the flagged ReadmeDropdown toggle boundary.

Don't add a second self-hosted family. IBM Plex Sans at two weights covers every role already in use; a display/editorial face would contradict PRODUCT.md's backend-engineer-not-design-agency positioning.
Don't add card-style shadows or background-tinted surfaces to inline content - the build's depth model is flat-plus-hairline-border everywhere except the two modal/overlay surfaces.
